summary: Repository rules have been hardened and passed eight Firestore emulator scenarios. Live deployed rules, bucket access and server IAM have not been verified, so this is not a production security certification.

findings.issue: Previously, raw visible CMS records were publicly readable even when they included attachment/source metadata.
findings.recommendation: Resolved in source: public clients must use sanitized Worker APIs; raw CMS reads require an administrator token.

findings.issue: Previously, owners could create or rewrite AI response status, usage metrics and session payloads directly from the browser.
findings.recommendation: Resolved in source: generation and feedback writes use verified Worker routes only.

findings.issue: Administrator browser writes could bypass the new atomic commerce/catalogue repository invariants.
findings.recommendation: Resolved in source: financial and CMS writes are server-only; server service-account access is governed by IAM.

findings.issue: Profile creation used a denylist and client activity fields lacked bounded scalar schemas.
findings.recommendation: Resolved in source: allowlisted fields, owner checks, immutable identities, bounded strings/scalars and boolean-only notification read updates.

findings.issue: The active production/preview rules and bucket IAM have not been retrieved or deployed in this session. Client-originated activity still needs operational abuse monitoring and retention.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the verified rules to the intended Firebase project, inspect bucket access and service-account permissions, then verify genuine account/asset flows before release.
